baselineRegression.method: Fifteen targeted final component tests against an isolated turn-start Settings copy; dependencies are mocked. Thirteen parameterized cases fail, two preserved-behavior cases pass. Failures can stop at their first assertion and do not represent thirteen independent defects. Eighteen other cases excluded from the baseline-only run.

changes: Cloud/local provider, reasoning-route, world-model and retrieval tests share operation state, immediate duplicate locking and cancellation ownership. Busy status is derived, and obsolete operations cannot clear a newer operation or report results after edits/unmount/account changes.

Generation, world and retrieval preference pages share load/PUT/confirmation handling, replacing three duplicated request/parsing/state implementations. Empty/missing top-level confirmations and explicit failure envelopes are rejected. Editing invalidates pending view updates while preserving the new draft.

Retrieval testing holds one operation from save through test; save rejection, edit or unmount prevents its continuation. Test results require ok:true and embedding data. Save/test buttons share the same busy guard.

Ordered/automatic reasoning-route tests save the visible route through the existing AppContext queue before testing the persisted route. Pinned tests continue to send explicit provider/model directly. Failed saves or an invalidated view do not launch the route test.

Reasoning drafts no longer reset because fallback array identity changed. A previous save confirmation cannot overwrite newer model/fallback edits; a provider switch still synchronizes the form. World inheritance derives its current model from confirmed vision context instead of the one-time resolved preference snapshot.
Image, video and image-to-video provider changes reuse one setter, preserving role-specific options, saved models, image auto mode and the separately configured image-edit role.
preserved: Existing setting entry points, role defaults and supported providers; authenticated API transport and backend routes.
Fixed, ordered-fallback and auto routing policy; independent generation roles; local/cloud provider credential and discovery behavior.
All previous prune40–51 changes as verified by their latest recorded fingerprints.
limitations: Component tests execute production expressions with mocked dependencies. Four existing tests mount the real AppProvider; there is no complete Settings-to-AppProvider-to-live-server/native-client acceptance in this batch.
No real model/API calls, visual acceptance, latency benchmark, full-suite run, backend source change, backend rebuild, client restart, commit or push. No real user preferences or data were modified.

Client aborts cannot undo accepted server writes. Separate pages/windows/clients are not coordinated by a database transaction; an acknowledged save followed by another client write can change what a persisted-route test uses.

Shared read/save requests have a 15-second signal and tests a 60-second signal. Reasoning saves still use the AppContext queue, whose 15-second timeout starts when dequeued and cannot be canceled by this panel; a pending accepted save may finish after closing. These signals do not guarantee server-side inference termination.

Preference confirmation validation checks required top-level fields, not full nested schemas. Initial load failure still exposes the default/existing draft after showing an error; a safe reload/retry gate remains to be designed.
Model browser caches are not account-keyed. Case-write coalescing, personal-case cache isolation and other program partitions remain open.
